This document words from 'data' after exclusions have been applied.

```{r}

library(ggplot2)

df <- as.data.frame(table(data$law))
colnames(df) <- c("Response", "Count")

# calculate percentages
df$Percentage <- df$Count / sum(df$Count) * 100

law <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Response, y = Percentage, fill = Response)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%")),  
            vjust = -0.5, size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Have you heard of the 'Digital Imprints Regime'?",
       x = "", y = "Percentage") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +     # <- use this OR the scale_... limits above
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")

ggsave("figures/law_change.png",
       plot = law,
       width = 8.27, height = 5.7, units = "in",
       dpi = 300, bg = "white")

```

## Normative, cognitive and affective perceptions of imprints

```{r}

likert_numeric <- function(response) {
  # handle factors
  if (is.factor(response)) response <- as.character(response)

  # trim / lowercase
  response_cleaned <- tolower(trimws(response))

  # mapping
  mapping <- c(
    "strongly disagree" = 1,
    "disagree" = 2,
    "somewhat disagree" = 3,
    "neither agree nor disagree" = 4,
    "somewhat agree" = 5,
    "agree" = 6,
    "strongly agree" = 7
  )

  # vectorised lookup (returns NA for non-matches or NA inputs)
  out <- unname(mapping[response_cleaned])
  as.numeric(out)
}

# numeric scale

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      ends_with(c("_norm", "_use", "_trust")),
      likert_numeric
    )
  )

# plot as a distribution

long <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(imprint_norm, imprint_use, imprint_trust,
             donation_norm, donation_use, donation_trust) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(imprint_norm, imprint_use, imprint_trust,
             donation_norm, donation_use, donation_trust),
    names_to = c("topic", "type"),
    names_pattern = "(imprint|donation)_(norm|use|trust)",
    values_to = "score"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    topic = recode(topic,
                   imprint  = "Digital imprints",
                   donation = "Campaign finance"),
    type = factor(type,
                  levels = c("norm", "use", "trust"),
                  labels = c("Importance", "Usefulness", "Reassurance")),
    score = as.numeric(score)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(score))

p_violin <- ggplot(long, aes(x = topic, y = score, fill = topic)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, width = 0.85, alpha = 0.7, color = NA) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ type, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7, limits = c(1, 7),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.04))) +
  labs(
    title = "Distributions of Likert Responses (1–7)",
    x = NULL, y = "Response (1–7)", fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")

p_violin

```

```{r}

# 1) Put Digital imprints on the LEFT, Campaign finance on the RIGHT
long <- long %>%
  mutate(
    topic = factor(topic, levels = c("Digital imprints", "Campaign finance"))
  )

# 2) Violin: smoother shape with higher `adjust` (e.g., 1.6–2.2 for Likert)
p_violin <- ggplot(long, aes(x = topic, y = score, fill = topic)) +
  geom_violin(
    trim = TRUE,
    adjust = 2.0,     # ↑ makes the density smoother (less wavy)
    width = 0.85,
    alpha = 0.7,
    color = NA
  ) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", size = 2.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ type, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.04))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +  # clip to Likert range without warnings
  labs(
    title = "Distributions of Likert Responses (1–7)",
    x = NULL, y = "Response (1–7)", fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2")

p_violin

```

```{r}

p_box <- ggplot(long, aes(x = topic, y = score, fill = topic)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.55,
    linewidth = 0.5,          # thin, crisp outlines
    fatten = 1.2,             # slightly thicker median line
    outlier.shape = 21,       # hollow circles for outliers
    outlier.size = 1.6,
    outlier.stroke = 0.4,
    outlier.fill = "white"
  ) +
  # mean marker (small white dot with outline)
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean, geom = "point",
    shape = 21, size = 2.2, stroke = 0.6,
    fill = "white", color = "black"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ type, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 1:7,
    limits = c(1, 7),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.06))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = NULL, y = "Distribution", fill = NULL
  ) +
  # colorblind-safe Okabe–Ito palette
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Digital imprints"  = "#0072B2",  # blue
    "Campaign finance"  = "#E69F00"   # orange
  )) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 6)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 4))
  )

p_box

```

```{r}

# custom colours
navy_hex  <- "#1F3A93"   # navy
dorg_hex  <- "#D35400"   # dark orange

p_violin_wiggly <- ggplot(long, aes(x = topic, y = score, fill = topic)) +
  geom_violin(
    trim   = FALSE,   # keep full tails
    adjust = 1.2,     # < 1 gives more “wiggly” detail
    width  = 0.85,
    alpha  = 0.7,
    color  = NA       # no hard outline
  ) +
  # median line for reference (thin, unobtrusive)
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar",
               width = 0.5, fatten = 1, linewidth = 0.35, color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ type, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = 1:7,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.04))
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 7)) +  # show full Likert range without warnings
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = NULL, y = "Distribution", fill = NULL
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Digital imprints" = navy_hex,
    "Campaign finance" = dorg_hex
  )) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )

p_violin_wiggly

# save to PNG, white background
ggsave("figures/violin_likert.png", 
       plot = p_violin_wiggly,

       dpi = 300, 
       bg = "white")
```

## Text response

```{r}

text_df <- data %>%
  dplyr::select(purpose) %>%
  filter(!is.na(purpose))

words <- text_df %>%
  tidytext::unnest_tokens(word, purpose)

data("stop_words")  # built-in
custom_stop <- c("library", "save", "promoted", "paid", "promoting", "provide", "promotes", "promote")
words_clean <- words %>%
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") %>%    # remove common stop words
  filter(!word %in% custom_stop)  

word_counts <- words_clean %>%
  count(word, sort = TRUE)

head(word_counts, 20)   # top 20 words

words <- word_counts %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 30) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(word, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Most Frequent Words in Free Text Responses",
       x = "Word", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

ggsave("figures/top_words.png", plot = words,
       width = 8.27, height = 5.7, units = "in", 
       dpi = 300, 
       bg = "white")

words

```
